question.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$E=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 7 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,E-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
E-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & -2-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 7-\lambda  & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(E-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Since the determinant of a triangular (or diagonal) matrix is given by the product of the entries on the main diagonal, we obtain the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}det(E-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & -2-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 7-\lambda  & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(-2-\lambda )(7-\lambda )(2-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (\lambda -1)(\lambda +2)(\lambda -7)(\lambda -2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$
